sections.name: normalizeTextForATS
sections.title: Cleaning resume text
sections.what: Replaces fancy punctuation, special spaces and invisible characters with plain versions and trims the ends, so resumes parse cleanly.
sections.why: Applicant tracking systems often misread curly quotes, long dashes and hidden characters.
sections.watch_out: Some replaced characters may not show in the packet, so check the file directly before editing.

sections.name: validateATS
sections.title: Checking resume text for problems
sections.what: Scans resume text and returns plain-language warnings for problem characters, including how many em dashes were found.
sections.why: Lets the app warn the user before a resume is exported.
sections.watch_out: It does not check bullets or special spaces, which the cleaning step does fix.

summary: Cleans resume text so applicant tracking systems read it correctly, and reports characters that could cause parsing problems.
purpose: Stops fancy punctuation and hidden characters from breaking how a resume is read by hiring software.
why: The header says the logic was ported from another project named career-ops. It also states the goal: strip characters that break ATS parsers.
how: 1. The normalize function swaps fancy dashes, quotes, ellipses, special spaces and bullets for plain versions, and removes invisible characters. 2. The validate function scans for the same kinds of characters and returns plain-language warnings, including a count of em dashes.
outputs: Cleaned text from the normalize function, and a list of warning messages from the validate function. An empty list means nothing was found.
risks: Some replacement patterns look blank in the packet view, so I cannot confirm which exact characters they match. The validate function does not check bullets or special spaces, so text can pass validation and still be changed by normalize.
debug: Compare the input text with the cleaned output to see what changed. If a warning appears for a character you cannot see, check the character in the source file.
